statement: Every GCP benchmark VM is created with a provider-enforced lifetime bound rendered from one shared definition (test/distributed/harness/gcp-vm-lifetime.js): a required whole-second maximum run duration with DELETE on expiry and boot-disk auto-deletion. Both GCP VM creators carry it: the six-name creation call of docs/benchmarks/cloud/provision-gcp.sh (VM_MAX_RUN_DURATION_SECONDS) and every Pulumi instance of GCPProvisioner (gcp.maxRunDurationSeconds in each caller's config). An absent or malformed bound is refused before any provider call; there is no unbounded creation path, and a create-only bound cannot obstruct placement or teardown.

constraints.statement: Change the two existing GCP VM creators (docs/benchmarks/cloud/provision-gcp.sh create and test/distributed/harness/gcp-provisioner.js) and their existing witnesses, and add exactly one shared lifetime definition both render. Preserve the six named VMs and existing identity, SSH, image, storage, firewall, placement and teardown owners. Add no scheduler, billing API, retry loop or competing cleanup authority. Root owns integration metadata and lifecycle records.

The lifetime bound is required at creation. provision-gcp.sh reads VM_MAX_RUN_DURATION_SECONDS and GCPProvisioner reads its config's maxRunDurationSeconds; each must be a positive whole number of seconds, else creation is refused before any gcloud or Pulumi call. Every VM is created with --max-run-duration=<seconds>s / scheduling.maxRunDuration, instance termination action DELETE and boot-disk auto-deletion, rendered by the one shared definition. Google owns the admissible range. No path creates a VM without the bound and no fallback drops it; placement and teardown ignore this create-only input.

Retain the draft and original evidence. Establish the red observation at unchanged source 4b0c8ec1de59e9a074afa97ce260afb2868685c5 with exactly the candidate witness bytes. Require actual successful script execution, the create call and all six argv names before the missing termination-argument assertion. A missing receipt, import error, fixture failure, command-not-found or nonzero exit alone is not this measurement. Invoke the real start lifecycle only after inspecting genuine failed receipt and full original output; never fabricate sealedAt or a red result.

Use scripts/quest-evidence/harness-runtime.js to execute the ordinary complete classified provisioner suite and produce the required receipt, including the exact test digest. Retain first-run full classified stdout/stderr, complete per-file TAP/stderr, source identities and actual recorded create argv. Keep the same witness and assertions in baseline and candidate. The managed proof records real process outcomes; independent review must inspect behavioral engagement and healthy ordinary create/place/teardown controls.

The Bash witness executes the real entrypoint with its existing gcloud and placement-node substitutes (the lifetime rendering runs on the real node); the provisioner witness runs the real Pulumi stack program against a recording @pulumi/gcp stand-in. Passing establishes local argument forwarding, validation and existing control behavior. It does not establish live provider acceptance, scheduling, deletion, billing closure or a successful GCP comparative campaign. No cloud resources are created to satisfy this unit.

A later authorized live launch must read back each VM's requested and effective termination state and boot-disk autoDelete before placement. Existing canonical teardown remains responsible after success, partial creation and failure; closure separately checks stopped VMs, disks and firewall. This unit grants no spending authority and does not extend the allocation lifetime or replace those obligations.
